I confirmed this diff directly between post_intro (buggy order) and post_benign (fixed: busy-wait moved inside the still-held prior_lock, so a later writer cannot even begin its own retire-order check until the earlier writer has verified safety). I first tried the project's own test/threadstest.c torture_rcu_high2 (the only in-repo test exercising >3 QPs, itself added by the fix PR) scaled up heavily (TSAN, 8 QPs, 32 readers, 550k+ cycles) without any report, then built a deterministic instrumented harness that proved the underlying invariant violation (two writer generations assigned/retiring one physical qp) occurs only in post_intro -- but per guidance that alone isn't sufficient for a memory-safety verdict, so I escalated to a harness (/poc/poc_orch3.c) with many concurrent ordinary RCU readers (each holding a derefed pointer across a short, realistic sleep) racing against many fast writers on the same small (4-slot) qp pool. This reliably produces a genuine AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free in post_intro (2/2 runs via run_poc) where a filler writer's premature ossl_synchronize_rcu() return lets it free data a concurrent reader is still using, and reliably does NOT reproduce in pre_intro or post_benign (2/2 clean runs each) using the exact same reproducer invoked identically via run_poc on all three versions.

oracle.description: /poc/poc_orch3.c + /poc/run.sh, run via run_poc identically on pre_intro, post_intro and post_benign. Links directly against the built libcrypto and drives the internal RCU API (ossl_rcu_lock_new(4, NULL) i.e. >3 QPs, the bug's documented precondition: "can cause use-after-free errors, but only if more than 3 QPs are allocated"). 8 fast "filler" writer threads continuously CRYPTO_zalloc a small tagged struct, ossl_rcu_assign_ptr it in, ossl_synchronize_rcu(), then CRYPTO_free the previous value; 12 "victim" threads each repeatedly take an ossl_rcu_read_lock, ossl_rcu_deref the current pointer, publish their own new value via a write, sleep briefly (0.2-3.2ms, simulating an ordinary straggler reader), then re-read the originally-derefed pointer before unlocking -- a completely legitimate RCU read-side usage pattern (hold a derefed pointer across a short critical section). Compiled with the same sanitizer flags as the official build (-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all) directly against /work's already-built libcrypto.a.
oracle.target_evidence: crypto/threads_pthread.c, ossl_synchronize_rcu(): in post_intro, the retire-order signal (next_to_retire++ / pthread_cond_broadcast / pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock->prior_lock)) happens BEFORE the busy-wait loop confirming qp->users==0; in post_benign the identical busy-wait is moved INSIDE the still-held prior_lock critical section, i.e. strictly before the increment/broadcast/unlock. This exactly matches meta.json's root_cause. Because prior_lock is released early in post_intro, a writer can race through its own retire-order gate and complete update_qp()/retire_qp() independently of another, still-active straggler reader elsewhere; with the pool capped at group_count=4 (">3 QPs") qp slots cycling in a tight circular buffer under heavy writer contention, this lets a filler's ossl_synchronize_rcu() call return -- and its caller CRYPTO_free() the just-superseded data -- while a concurrent victim thread's earlier ossl_rcu_read_lock()/ossl_rcu_deref() reference to that exact data is still live and about to be re-read. AddressSanitizer catches exactly this: READ of size 8 at .../poc_orch3.c:103 in victim_thread_fn, on memory "freed by thread T.. CRYPTO_free /work/crypto/mem.c:353 / filler_writer_fn /poc/poc_orch3.c:64", "previously allocated by ... CRYPTO_zalloc ... filler_writer_fn /poc/poc_orch3.c:51". Identical reproducer run via run_poc: post_intro crashed=True with this heap-use-after-free on 2/2 runs; pre_intro and post_benign both completed cleanly (crashed=False, "DONE: no crash observed") on 2/2 runs each.
